evidence.quote: expansion of the buccal and lingual cortical plates related to the lower molars area

Intraoral examination revealed expansion of the buccal and lingual cortical plates related to the lower molars area with nonhealing mucosa due to the previous incisions. On palpation, a firm bony mass was felt. No fluctuation of mucosa or crackling was detected. There was no clinical evidence of cervical lymphadenopathy at the time of presentation. Cone-beam computed tomography scan showed a large radiolucency with indefinite margins related to the lower right molar area, with involvement of the inferior alveolar nerve (Fig. 2). PET scan did not reveal any evidence of distant metastasis.

fields.subject: index_patient
fields.name: Incisional biopsy
fields.indication: diagnostic evaluation of large painful mandibular mass

evidence.quote: An incisional biopsy was performed.

A 62-year-old female Egyptian patient attended to the outpatient clinic of the Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery Department, Cairo University in October 2022, complaining of a large painful swelling related to the right mandibular molar area (Fig. 1). The patient reported to have this swelling for 2 months. The swelling was initially diagnosed as a periapical abscess and was mistreated by teeth extractions, multiple incisions, and suturing by the general practitioner. The patient was in good physical health status, without any known health condition or any genetic disorder detected, also with no history of irradiation.

Intraoral examination revealed expansion of the buccal and lingual cortical plates related to the lower molars area with nonhealing mucosa due to the previous incisions. On palpation, a firm bony mass was felt. No fluctuation of mucosa or crackling was detected. There was no clinical evidence of cervical lymphadenopathy at the time of presentation. Cone-beam computed tomography scan showed a large radiolucency with indefinite margins related to the lower right molar area, with involvement of the inferior alveolar nerve (Fig. 2). PET scan did not reveal any evidence of distant metastasis.

An incisional biopsy was performed. Histopathological examination of hematoxylin and eosin-stained sections revealed sheets of round cells with an indistinct cellular outline. The cells had round-to-oval hyperchromatic nuclei, scanty cytoplasm, and distinct nuclear boundaries (Fig. 3). The malignant stroma had minimal osteoid deposition (Fig. 4).

fields.name: SATB2
fields.specimen: incisional biopsy of right mandibular tumor

evidence.quote: The diffuse-positive nuclear immunohistochemical staining (IHC) of special AT-rich sequence-binding protein 2 (SATB2) marker confirmed the diagnosis of SCOS (Figs. 5 and 6).

An incisional biopsy was performed. Histopathological examination of hematoxylin and eosin-stained sections revealed sheets of round cells with an indistinct cellular outline. The cells had round-to-oval hyperchromatic nuclei, scanty cytoplasm, and distinct nuclear boundaries (Fig. 3). The malignant stroma had minimal osteoid deposition (Fig. 4).

The diffuse-positive nuclear immunohistochemical staining (IHC) of special AT-rich sequence-binding protein 2 (SATB2) marker confirmed the diagnosis of SCOS (Figs. 5 and 6). It was performed to exclude other small round cell tumors that occur in old age [] such as non-Hodgkin lymphoma, small cell neuroendocrine carcinomas, poorly differentiated synovial sarcoma, and metastatic small cell carcinoma [, ].

facts.clinical_statement: Diffuse-positive nuclear SATB2 staining

fields.subject: index_patient
fields.name: Ewing sarcoma
fields.diagnostic_basis: author interpretation of positive SATB2 immunohistochemistry in small-round-cell tumor differential

evidence.quote: In our case, it was used to rule out the other undifferentiated round cell sarcomas such as Ewing and the so-called Ewing-like sarcoma, and rhabdomyosarcoma (these previous tumors usually occur in the pediatric age) [, ].

The diffuse-positive nuclear immunohistochemical staining (IHC) of special AT-rich sequence-binding protein 2 (SATB2) marker confirmed the diagnosis of SCOS (Figs. 5 and 6). It was performed to exclude other small round cell tumors that occur in old age [] such as non-Hodgkin lymphoma, small cell neuroendocrine carcinomas, poorly differentiated synovial sarcoma, and metastatic small cell carcinoma [, ].

SCOS stain positively to considerable number of IHC markers such as CD99, vimentin, osteocalcin, osteonectin, and cytokeratin [, , ]. These markers also stain several round cell tumors. The special AT-rich sequence-binding protein 2 (SATB2) is an important transcription factor for osteoblastogenesis and is considered a highly sensitive marker for osteoblast lineage differentiation. In our case, it was used to rule out the other undifferentiated round cell sarcomas such as Ewing and the so-called Ewing-like sarcoma, and rhabdomyosarcoma (these previous tumors usually occur in the pediatric age) [, ]. Moreover, the positive staining helped us to exclude other round cell tumors that share various degrees of similarity with SCOS like non-Hodgkin lymphoma, metastatic small cell melanoma, poorly differentiated synovial sarcoma, small cell carcinoma, neuroblastoma, and mesenchymal chondrosarcoma [].

facts.clinical_statement: Diagnostic consideration excluded using SATB2: Ewing sarcoma
facts.notes: Authors’ stated differential exclusions, not a new independent test result.

The special AT-rich sequence-binding protein 2 (SATB2) is an important transcription factor for osteoblastogenesis and is considered a highly sensitive marker for osteoblast lineage differentiation. In our case, it was used to rule out the other undifferentiated round cell sarcomas such as Ewing and the so-called Ewing-like sarcoma, and rhabdomyosarcoma (these previous tumors usually occur in the pediatric age) [, ]. Moreover, the positive staining helped us to exclude other round cell tumors that share various degrees of similarity with SCOS like non-Hodgkin lymphoma, metastatic small cell melanoma, poorly differentiated synovial sarcoma, small cell carcinoma, neuroblastoma, and mesenchymal chondrosarcoma [].

summary.text: A 62-year-old woman described as Egyptian presented in October 2022 with two months of painful right mandibular swelling. An initial abscess diagnosis had led to extractions, incisions and suturing, with persistent nonhealing mucosa. She had no other known medical or genetic disorder and no irradiation history. Examination showed cortical expansion and a firm mass without fluctuation, crackling or cervical lymphadenopathy.

CBCT showed an ill-defined radiolucent mandibular lesion involving the inferior alveolar nerve; PET found no distant metastases. Biopsy showed small round malignant cells, scant osteoid and diffuse nuclear SATB2 positivity, supporting small cell osteosarcoma. The abscess label was incorrect and the authors excluded other round-cell tumors. Diagnostic molecular testing was not performed.

Hemimandibulectomy achieved a clear 10-mm margin, with a reconstruction plate followed six months later by a free fibula microvascular flap. No adjuvant chemotherapy or radiotherapy was given. Resection pathology/IHC matched the biopsy, and no clinical recurrence was seen through manuscript preparation; the exact follow-up duration was not reported.
